subject: System Design
title: Consistent Hashing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Consistent Hashing.

hook.text: You add a fourth server to a three-server cluster. With naive hashing, 75% of keys get remapped. Chaos.

buildup.text: Consistent hashing maps keys and nodes onto a ring. Each key goes to the next node clockwise on the ring.

discovery.text: Adding a node only remaps keys between it and its neighbor — about 1/N of the total, not nearly all.

twist.text: Basic consistent hashing creates uneven distribution. Virtual nodes — multiple positions per server — fix this.

climax.text: Consistent hashing powers DynamoDB, Cassandra, and every major distributed cache and database.

punchline.text: Add or remove nodes without remapping everything.

quiz.question: What problem does consistent hashing solve?
options: Minimizes key remapping when nodes are added or removed
